newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger won't speculate on duration of talks.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger won't speculate on duration of talks.

text.p: New Zealand's caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Thursday he would not speculate on when coaltiion talks would produce a new government.

"My view is very clear. We should take the time necessary to do the job properly. I am not concerned about time in that sense. It is just a matter of progressing the talks in a sensible fashion and making certain we produce the best possible government for New Zealand," he told journalists as he went into the seventh round of talks with nationalist New Zealand First.
Asked if there would be a government before December 13, the latest date Parliament can meet, Bolger said: "I won't even speculate on that."

Bolger's conservative National Party currently leads a caretaker government after a general election on October 12 left NZ First with the balance of power. NZ First is negotiating separately with both National and the main opposition Labour party over the shape of the new government.
Peters said on Wednesday he could not forecast whether New Zealand First would isolate one prospective coalition partner by December 13.
Peters and NZ First's key policy analyst MP Peter McCardle did not attend Thursday's negotiations with National. A spokesman said Peters was doing background work on the talks.
NZ First is due to meet Labour on Thursday at 2 p.m. for the last formal talks of the week. Informal talks will continue on Friday, Peters' spokesman said.
